rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 5-6, the authors build and test their own ESP32 drip system with a SEN0308 capacitive soil moisture sensor in a container of potting soil in Qatar; they report sensor calibration tests (Tables 2-4), dripper flow rates (Table 5) and one week of soil moisture, humidity and temperature logs (Figures 20-22).
rows.notes: The study does use the SEN0308 sensor, but it reports no water-savings result: there is no control or conventional-irrigation comparison and no percentage saving. Section 6 only computes that the automated system applied 0.676 gallons per onion bulb over a week, close to a recommended 0.623 gallons, and concludes the system provides adequate moisture. The 11% water saving in the passage is not from this study (it may come from the other cited reference). Delivering an appropriate amount of water automatically is at most a precondition of water conservation, so upstream is set true. Single container, one week, no replication, no dispersion statistics, no stated requirements or limitations on a savings effect.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 5-6, own prototype build and field test of a SEN0308-based automated drip system growing spring onions in a container; one week of logged sensor data (Figures 20-22) and flow measurements (Table 5).
rows.notes: No yield is measured and no 12.05% yield increase appears in the study. The only crop-related result (Section 6, Figure 18) is a qualitative observation that after one week spring onions had begun to grow from a few onion bulbs and the plants looked healthy; there is no control treatment, no harvest, no yield quantification. This is at most a precondition (the system can sustain plant growth) rather than evidence of a yield increase, so upstream is set true. Single container, one crop, one week, no replication, no uncertainty measures.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is an engineering prototype paper (ESP32 + SEN0308 + Blynk) tested in one acrylic container of potting soil for about a week in Qatar; it validates sensors against a thermal camera and a weather website and measures dripper flow rates, but contains no water-savings or yield comparison. The quantitative figures in the passage (11% water saving, 12.05% yield increase) do not originate from this study.
